chapters.category: Aramaic and Ethiopic textual traditions • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 77 — The Four Winds, Seven Mountains and Seven Rivers
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. The Hasmonean-period Aramaic manuscript 4Q210 (4QEnastrᶜ ar), fragment 1 ii lines 14–18, together with the overlapping Aramaic manuscript 4Q209 (4QEnastrᵇ ar), fragment 23, is primary for the surviving wording associated with the opening designations of east, south, west and north in verses 1–4. Their lacunae and their sequence where it differs from the later form remain unsupplied. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, preserves the full eight-verse chapter and supplies the north's three divisions and the vision of seven mountains, rivers and islands. Earlier legible Aramaic readings are followed where they directly correspond; Geʽez supplies the complete sequence and all wording not extant in Aramaic. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: They call the first wind East, because it is first.
verses.study: The east receives its name from priority and sunrise. The shortest saying in the chapter roots direction in ordered beginning.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:8 — the garden is planted toward the east at the beginning
Matthew 24:27 — lightning shines from east to west

verses.text: They call the second wind South, because the Great One dwells there, and there the One blessed forever has his dwelling.
verses.study: The south is associated with the dwelling of the Great and Blessed One. Geography becomes a reverent way of speaking about divine presence.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 33:2 — the Lord comes from Sinai with holy splendor
Habakkuk 3:3 — God comes from Teman in the south

verses.text: The western wind is named Diminishing, because there all the lights of heaven decrease and go down.
verses.study: The west is named for the visible decline and setting of the lights. Its designation turns repeated observation into remembered instruction.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:19 — the sun knows its time for setting
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun sets and returns toward its rising

verses.text: The fourth wind, called North, is divided into three parts. One is for the dwelling of people; another is for seas of water, lakes, trees, rivers, darkness and clouds; and the third is for the Paradise of Righteousness.
verses.study: The north's three regions encompass human habitation, waters and landscape, and the Paradise of Righteousness. The division joins ordinary dwelling with distant and sacred geography.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:8–10 — the garden and its river belong to sacred geography
Ezekiel 47:1–12 — life-giving waters flow through a transformed landscape

verses.text: I saw seven high mountains, taller than all the mountains on the earth. From them hoarfrost goes out, while days, seasons and years pass and proceed.
verses.study: The seven mountains stand above earthly ranges and are linked with hoarfrost and passing time. Enduring landmarks are set beside the movement of days and years.
crossReferences: Job 38:29 — frost is spoken of as coming forth by birth
Psalm 90:2 — God's eternity precedes the mountains and the world

verses.text: I saw seven rivers upon the earth, greater than all the rivers. One of them comes from the west, and its water pours into the Great Sea.
verses.study: The vision turns from mountains to a sevenfold survey of rivers. The first river is traced by direction and destination.
crossReferences: Genesis 2:10 — a river flows out to water the garden
Ecclesiastes 1:7 — rivers run toward the sea

verses.text: Two come from the north to the sea, and their waters pour into the Erythraean Sea in the east. The remaining four go out along the side of the north: two toward their own sea, the Erythraean Sea, and two flow into the Great Sea, where it is said there is a wilderness.
verses.study: The remaining rivers connect north, east, the Erythraean Sea, the Great Sea and wilderness. Their branching courses extend the chapter's ordered map.
crossReferences: Numbers 34:3–12 — boundaries are described through seas and directional limits
Psalm 107:23–24 — the great waters display the works of the Lord

verses.text: I saw seven great islands in the sea and on the earth: two on the earth and five in the Great Sea.
verses.study: The count closes with seven islands distributed between land and the Great Sea. The chapter repeatedly gathers the world's variety into numbered order.
crossReferences: Isaiah 42:10 — the islands and those who inhabit them join creation's praise
Psalm 97:1 — the many coastlands rejoice before the Lord's reign

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 77 begins by naming the four directional winds. East is first, south is associated with divine dwelling, west with the setting lights, and north with three distinct regions.

The northern division moves from human habitation through seas, lakes, trees, rivers, darkness and clouds to the Paradise of Righteousness. The vision places familiar and sacred spaces within one ordered world.
Seven mountains introduce the chapter's geography of sevens. Their height and frost stand beside days, seasons and years that continue to pass.

Seven rivers and seven islands complete the survey. Direction, destination and number make the created world intelligible and preserve Enoch's received observations without turning them into a modern map.

crossReferences: Genesis 2:8–14 — garden, rivers and lands form sacred geography
Job 38:22–30 — frost and waters belong to divine ordering
Psalm 90:1–4 — mountains endure while generations and time pass
Psalm 104:19 — the sun knows its setting
Ecclesiastes 1:5–7 — sun, wind and rivers follow recurring courses
Isaiah 42:10–12 — coastlands and the ends of the earth give praise
